A check the compiler inserts at a core-language operation that can have undefined behavior, evaluated like a C++26 contract assertion on the operation's precondition.
The mode that decides what happens when a check's predicate is false: ignore, observe, enforce, quick-enforce, or assume.
Call the violation handler; on a normal return, continue past the violation.
The observe outcome for the priced slice: proceed past a state the language does not define.
A non-portable build option, macro, or flag by which one implementation offers a behavior without the standard requiring it.
The ongoing cost a standardized feature imposes on the rest of the standard and its implementations for as long as it exists.
Net present value delivered per unit of specification and maintenance capacity spent.
Marginal benefit per beneficiary per year of the standardized guarantee, measured against what a vendor opt-in already delivers
Length in years of the adoption window over which N(t) is non-negligible
Fraction of value forfeited to ossification once the design is frozen, 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1
Specification and interaction complexity the slice spends
Annual cost per unit of complexity imposed on everything standardized around it
The return, per unit of specification and maintenance capacity, of the best alternative use of that capacity; λ ≥ 0, since capacity can always be left unspent
